documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics and gynecology group. Routine prenatal visit 05/11/2026, 36w0d.

32-year-old G1 with type 1 diabetes, celiac disease and recurrent iron deficiency anemia. Pregnancy has gone smoothly; prenatal labs all normal and glucose well controlled on insulin with endocrinology. She came in today worried that she might end up needing a cesarean.

Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro per scale, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, ibuprofen 400 mg as needed (on her list, not in use), aspirin 81 mg, folic acid, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate. NKDA.
Social: never smoker, alcohol none in pregnancy, preschool teacher.

BP 120/78. BMI 30.
Fetal heart rate 140.
Ultrasound today: breech presentation.

Assessment: 36 weeks, breech presentation, pre-existing type 1 diabetes, otherwise uncomplicated.
Plan: discussed options. External cephalic version offered at 37 weeks on labor and delivery; she would like to try it, as she hopes to avoid a cesarean. If unsuccessful or the baby turns back, scheduled cesarean at 39 weeks. Weekly fetal testing continues.

documents.title: Labor and Delivery Procedure Note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Hospital birthing center, obstetric triage. 05/20/2026, 37w2d.
Procedure: external cephalic version for breech presentation.
Pre-procedure ultrasound: breech, normal fluid. Reactive nonstress test. Two attempts made under ultrasound guidance; fetus did not rotate. Procedure stopped.
Post-procedure monitoring 60 minutes: reassuring fetal heart tracing, no contractions, no bleeding.
Outcome: unsuccessful version. Scheduled cesarean delivery at 39w0d on 06/01/2026. Patient disappointed but comfortable with the plan.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Hospital birthing center.
Admitted 06/01/2026. Discharged 06/03/2026.

Admission diagnosis: intrauterine pregnancy at 39w0d, breech presentation after unsuccessful external cephalic version; pre-existing type 1 diabetes.
Procedure 06/01/2026: scheduled low transverse cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. Delivered a healthy girl, 3.2 kg, vigorous at birth, to the newborn nursery with her mother. Placenta delivered intact. Blood loss within the usual range for cesarean. No complications.
Diabetes: insulin infusion during surgery, then glargine and lispro back to her pre-pregnancy doses per endocrinology's written plan; glucose stable.
Course: uncomplicated. Tolerating diet, ambulating, voiding, incision clean and dry.

Discharge medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals per her pre-pregnancy scale; ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed; acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; cholecalciferol; calcium carbonate. Aspirin stopped at delivery.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: obstetrics incision check at 2 weeks, postpartum visit at 6 weeks; endocrinology in 2 weeks; PCP as scheduled.

documents.title: Baby is here
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just wanted to let you know our daughter arrived June 1! The version didn't work so it ended up being the planned C-section, but everything went fine. Home and recovering. Sugars are a roller coaster but endo is on it. Do I need to see you after my OB checks?

documents.title: RE: Baby is here
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations to you both! I'm so glad you're both well. Yes, let's see you in about 5 weeks to go over your iron, thyroid and diabetes labs and update your medication list. Front desk will send you a time. Call us any time before that if needed.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Postpartum check-in, 32F, 5.5 weeks after a scheduled cesarean (breech, ECV unsuccessful). Baby along in the car seat, doing well.

Recovering well. Incision healed per OB at 2 weeks, mild soreness only with lifting. Off the post-op ibuprofen and acetaminophen. Bleeding finished. Sleep broken but mood good, enjoying the baby, partner home for the summer; PHQ-9 3. Endo put her back on her pre-pregnancy insulin plan right after delivery, sugars settling, a couple of lows on night feeds that she treats. Aspirin stopped at delivery. Gluten-free, no GI symptoms. Asks if she can use ibuprofen again for cramps once periods return.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro per scale, ferrous sulfate 325 daily, cholecalciferol 2000 u daily, calcium carbonate 500 bid; finished folic acid. NKDA.

Exam: well appearing. BP and HR normal. Thyroid not enlarged, nontender. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, low transverse cesarean scar well healed, no erythema. No calf tenderness or edema.

A/P
1. Postpartum after cesarean for breech - healing well; breech and diabetes-in-pregnancy entries resolved. OB postpartum visit next week.
2. T1DM - back on pre-pregnancy insulin via endo. A1c today.
3. Recurrent IDA - CBC and ferritin today after delivery; continue ferrous sulfate.
4. Thyroid: TSH today given T1DM, celiac and family history, postpartum timing.
5. Celiac, vitamin D deficiency - stable on current plan.
6. Heavy menses/cramps - ibuprofen 400 prn back on her list.
7. Aspirin and folic acid off the list.
Follow-up mid-September, booked.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.2 and ferritin 22: lower than spring 2025 after the delivery but holding; continue daily iron and we'll recheck in September. A1c 6.6. TSH normal.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lauren, your blood count is 11.2 and iron stores are on the low side of normal after the delivery, so please keep taking the iron every day. Thyroid is normal and your A1c is 6.6. We'll repeat the blood count when I see you in September.

Medications: insulin glargine, insulin lispro, ferrous sulfate, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate. NKDA.
